ga.heading: General and administrative expenses
ga.text:
General and administrative expenses were $32.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $16.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of approximately $16.3 million, or 100.7%. The increase was primarily driven by an increase in employee compensation and benefits expenses of $9.7 million, and an increase in other general expenses of $6.6 million.

Employee compensation and benefits expenses were $18.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $9.7 million, or 109.0% from $8.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily due to headcount growth, to support growth in gross premiums written, share-based and compensation and incentive compensation.

Other general and administrative expenses were $13.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $6.6 million, or 91.3%, from $7.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This increase was primarily due to information technology expenses to support growth in gross premiums written, public company transition costs, an increase in sponsorships and corporate events, digital and print advertising expenses and increased merchant processing fees.

nonop.heading: Interest expense
nonop.text: Interest expense was $4.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $1.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of approximately $3.0 million or 183.3%. The increase was primarily due to higher average debt principal from recent debt transactions. For further information, see “Liquidity and Capital Resources and Changes in Financial Condition—Debt.”

pretax.text: Segment Adjusted EBITDA of each operating segment represents net income before interest expense, income tax expense, depreciation, software amortization, litigation and settlement, sponsorship fees and other non-recurring costs. For purposes of this measure, interest expense excludes amortization of debt issuance costs and unrealized losses on interest rate swap agreements, which are included in interest expense in our consolidated statements of operations.

tax.heading: (1) Assumes an effective tax rate of 27.9%
tax.text:
Because reserve estimates are based on incomplete information, changes in assumptions or emergence patterns can materially affect results in future periods. As claims mature and more information becomes available, we review and update our estimates, and any adjustments are recognized in current-period earnings as favorable or unfavorable prior-year reserve development. The liability is recorded in unpaid losses and LAE within the consolidated balance sheets in the Prospectus and condensed consolidated balance sheets in this Quarterly Report, and changes in the estimate are reflected in the consolidated statements of operations in the Prospectus and condensed consolidated statements of operations in this Quarterly Report.

Actual results may differ from these estimates due to changes in claim severity, frequency, or emergence patterns, particularly in periods impacted by catastrophic events or shifts in macroeconomic conditions.

For further information, see Note 8—“Liability For Unpaid Losses and Loss Adjustment Expenses” in our notes to the interim condensed consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q and in our notes to the condensed consolidated financial statements to the Prospectus.

net.heading: Net loss ratio
net.text:
Net loss ratio was 42.8% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 47.5% for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of 4.7 pp. This decrease was primarily due to more favorable reinsurance terms, which have improved as our underwriting results have produced positive outcomes for our reinsurance partners.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, catastrophe losses made up 21.4% of total losses, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 where catastrophe losses made up 33.9% of total losses. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, attritional losses made up 78.6% of total losses, whereas for the three months ended September 30, 2025, attritional losses made up 66.1% of total losses.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities was approximately $137.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $49.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $87.7 million. The increase was primarily driven by favorable changes in operating liabilities, partially offset by unfavorable changes in operating assets.

For purposes of this measure, interest expense excludes amortization of debt issuance costs and unrealized losses on interest rate swap agreements, which are included in interest expense in our consolidated statements of operations.

capex.text: We believe that our sources of liquidity and capital will be sufficient to finance our growth strategy and resulting operations, planned capital expenditures and the additional expenses we expect to incur as a public company for at least the next twelve months. However, we cannot assure you that cash provided by operating activities or cash and cash equivalents will be sufficient to meet our future needs. If we are unable to generate sufficient cash flows from operations in the future, we may have to obtain additional financing. We may also seek additional financing to pursue acquisitions or other strategic initiatives, or in light of favorable market conditions. If we obtain additional capital by issuing equity, the interests of our existing shareholders will be diluted. If we incur additional indebtedness, that indebtedness may contain significant financial and other covenants that may significantly restrict our operations. We cannot assure you that we could obtain additional financing on favorable terms or at all. See “Risk factors— R isks R elated to our L iquidity and A ccess to C apital —We may require additional capital in the future, which may not be available or may only be available on unfavorable terms.”

net sales.heading: Commission and fees revenue
net sales.text: Commission and fees revenue totaled approximately $75.1 million, which represents an increase of $29.4 million, or 64.4%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher policy-related fee and commission volumes driven by growth in policies and premiums written.

intro.text: Orion180 Insurance Group Inc. (Orion180) (NASDAQ: OIG) is a founder-led technology-focused, high growth, high-margin specialty insurance group delivering innovative insurance solutions with a growing footprint across the United States. Since beginning operations in 2018, they have organically grown to become the second largest excess and surplus (“E&S”) lines homeowners insurance provider in the United States by direct written premiums with a presence in 14 states. Their diverse product offerings across E&S and admitted homeowners’ insurance, private flood insurance, and a range of ancillary products are distributed through a network of approximately 17,000 active independent agents as of September 30, 2026.
